translationRepairs: He died and was posthumously titled Zhuangmin.
He died and was posthumously titled Zhuangque.
s0024 has 諡壯愨. 愨 is què, so Zhuangque is correct; Zhuangmin would require 愍 and is an unsupported misreading.
He died and was given the posthumous title Zhuangmin.
He died and was given the posthumous title Zhuangque.
The literal likewise renders 壯愨 as Zhuangmin; Zhuangque restores the correct reading of 愨 què.
In the twenty-seventh year he died at eighty-four; he was posthumously made Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and titled Zhuangmin.
In the twenty-seventh year he died at eighty-four; he was posthumously made Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and titled Zhuangque.
s0044 ends 諡壯愨. The rest of the sentence (death at eighty-four; 太子太保) is already accurate; only the posthumous-name reading needs Zhuangque, not Zhuangmin.
In the eighteenth year he died and was posthumously titled Gongmin.
In the eighteenth year he died and was posthumously titled Gongque.
s0070 has 諡恭愨. 愨 is què, so Gongque is correct; Gongmin misreads the same graph as 愍.
Frontier Commissioner Zhang Guangsi directed Wudang to assault Taigong, Daitai, and Xiong in separate columns, and all were captured.
Frontier Commissioner Zhang Guangsi directed Wudang to assault Taigong and Daitaixiong in separate columns, and they were captured.

分攻台拱大台雄 lists two targets: 台拱 (already Taigong in s0005) and 大台雄 as one place-name; splitting 大台雄 into Daitai and Xiong invents a third site. The proposed Taigong and Daitaixiong matches the Chinese without adding content.
